compute.body: Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, with capacity utilization at 81.7%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%, but utilization was lower at 72.2%. Output is rising in both industries, while the utilization gap indicates different pressure on installed capacity.
compute.headline: Compute output is growing under different capacity conditions

connectivity.body: The public map lists 168 active U.S. internet exchange points, the sites where networks exchange traffic. Despite the national exchange-point footprint, 19 states combine data-center development with limited visible public interconnection depth. Private routes and bilateral links may sit outside public records. The state count therefore measures visible public interconnection.
connectivity.headline: Public network visibility is uneven around data-center development

finance.body: At the measured level, operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.42 times, providing a substantial source of internal funding. Cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx, so cash alone falls just short of one year at the current spending rate. Borrower strain is 26.0, compared with lender strain of -13.5. The combination supports current spending from operations, but with a limited cash cushion and divergent conditions for borrowers and lenders.
finance.headline: Operations cover current CapEx, but reserves provide less than a year of coverage

macro.body: Market support has strengthened, but not evenly. The AI Equity Index rose materially to 35.9, while the share of companies with positive one-year returns edged up to 63.7% and the median return slipped to 13.1%. CNBC reported that Micron beat earnings estimates and issued strong guidance as data-center revenue increased elevenfold. That result shows substantial demand in one part of the hardware chain, but the market measures still point to uneven gains across the wider group. The investment cycle retains internal financial support: operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.42 times. Yet cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx, borrower strain stands at 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5. The physical side has a similar split. Electric-power construction grew 10.8%, but only 24.2% of the 2,061 GW active interconnection queue has reached an executed-agreement or construction stage. Spending and construction are active; the harder question is how much proposed capacity can clear financing and grid connection. Execution is also increasingly local. Available records contain 1,556 sites in development, about half the 3,068 operating sites. Construction Dive reports that public support is emerging as a data-center bottleneck, while the drought screen now places 24.4% of campuses with county data in counties containing some D2-or-worse drought; 22.2% are in counties where at least a quarter of the area is affected. County overlap does not establish site-level drought or water demand, and these developments do not show how many projects will be delayed. They reinforce why development-site counts should not be treated as completed capacity.
macro.headline: AI market pricing strengthens, but financing and physical execution remain uneven

market.body: The AI Equity Index rose materially to 35.9, while the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns increased only slightly to 63.7% and the median return slipped to 13.1%. The stronger index alongside softer typical performance indicates that gains remain uneven. CNBC reported that Micron beat earnings estimates and issued strong guidance as its data-center revenue increased elevenfold. That is a significant company-level result, but it does not establish broad earnings strength across the sector.
market.headline: Index strength runs ahead of broader returns

power.body: Commercial electricity demand growth increased slightly to 3.1%, while total retail demand growth eased to 1.2%. Net planned generation additions through the pipeline horizon slipped to 225.2 GW, and retail electricity price growth eased slightly to 4.4%. Google reportedly agreed to support nuclear uprates at Georgia Power's Vogtle and Hatch plants, providing one route to additional output from existing facilities. It does not establish when the wider planned pipeline will be delivered.
power.headline: Commercial electricity demand outpaces total demand as planned additions edge down

workforce.body: Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at just 0.8%. Two channels have positive real-earnings growth. Barron's reports an expectation that AI will create more jobs than layoffs, though with painful disruption. That is a forward-looking judgment; the current measures still show narrow gains across the tracked labor channels.
workforce.headline: Job-creation expectations run ahead of current labor breadth

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.8 and the median one-year return rose to 13.7%, but the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns slipped to 61.8%. Average sector trading pressure increased materially to 51.3. Together, the measures show positive performance for a majority of the group alongside greater pressure and narrower breadth. Barron's reported that Jabil shares fell despite a very strong AI-demand outlook, a company-level example of favorable demand commentary failing to lift the stock.

headline.text: Gains continue, but market participation narrows as trading pressure rises

body.text: Operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.42 times, while cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx at the current rate. Borrower strain is 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5, leaving a wide split between the two measures. Morningstar characterized AI financing partnerships as credit-positive for Nvidia and data-center operators. That is a favorable assessment for specific companies and arrangements, not evidence that financing conditions have improved across the measured borrower base.

headline.text: Cash flow covers current CapEx, but credit conditions remain uneven

body.text: Available records list 168 active U.S. internet exchange points with a combined 2,805 reported members. They also identify 90 international submarine cable systems and 115 U.S.-connected cable-catalog entries. These counts describe the visible network footprint, not its available bandwidth or route redundancy. Morningstar reported that Ekinops is supporting Bluebird Fiber's Midwest network investments as infrastructure demand grows. That provides a regional example of investment but no basis for estimating nationwide capacity growth.

headline.text: The visible U.S. network footprint spans domestic exchanges and international cables

body.text: Commercial electricity demand grew 3.1%, versus 1.2% for total retail demand, while retail prices rose 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW through the pipeline horizon. Separate queue data show 2,061 GW of active capacity, but only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages; historically, 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Utility Dive reported that MISO has proposed a fast-track study process for large loads and generation. The proposal addresses one stage of the conversion process, but it does not establish that connections or planned supply will arrive faster.

headline.text: Commercial electricity demand outpaces the total as grid planners seek faster studies

body.text: Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth. The strongest is power and communication construction, at 0.8%, and only two channels have positive real-earnings growth. CNBC reported that AI hiring is surging on Wall Street, indicating a concentrated source of demand outside the strongest tracked construction channel. The report does not alter the broader reading: employment gains remain narrow across the measured channels.

headline.text: AI hiring appears in pockets while measured job growth remains narrow
Investment momentum remains intact, while returns and infrastructure delivery remain selective

paragraphs.text: The market is still rewarding a majority of covered companies, but less uniformly. The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.8 and the median one-year return rose to 13.7%, while the share with positive returns slipped to 61.8% and average sector trading pressure increased materially to 51.3. Barron's reported that Jabil shares fell despite a very strong AI-demand outlook. That company-level reaction is consistent with a market in which favorable demand signals do not guarantee positive returns.

Corporate funding and industrial output remain supportive of the buildout. Operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.42 times, though cash reserves equal 0.96 years of CapEx and borrower strain stands at 26.0. Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, while semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%. Capacity utilization is 81.7% for computers and 72.2% for semiconductors, indicating that expansion is occurring under different capacity conditions.

Power remains a central execution test. Commercial electricity demand grew 3.1%, faster than total retail demand at 1.2%, while net planned generation additions stand at 225.2 GW. Separate queue data show 2,061 GW of active capacity, but only 24.2% has reached an executed-agreement or construction stage, and 13% of the 2000–2020 cohort ultimately reached operation. The planned-generation and queue measures cover different project sets, but both distinguish proposed capacity from delivered supply. MISO's proposed fast-track study process addresses this problem procedurally; it does not guarantee faster connections.

Broader economic diffusion remains partial. Businesses reporting current AI use account for 23.8%, and 27.6% expect to use it within six months. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, even as CNBC reports a surge in AI hiring on Wall Street. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.2% and real output grew 2.5%, but those aggregate results do not isolate an AI effect.

editorial_synthesis.instructions:
You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

diagnostics.text: Power remains a central execution test. Commercial electricity demand grew 3.1%, faster than total retail demand at 1.2%, while net planned generation additions stand at 225.2 GW. Separate queue data show 2,061 GW of active capacity, but only 24.2% has reached an executed-agreement or construction stage, and 13% of the 2000–2020 cohort ultimately reached operation. The planned-generation and queue measures cover different project sets, but both distinguish proposed capacity from delivered supply. MISO's proposed fast-track study process addresses this problem procedurally; it does not guarantee faster connections.
